meta.description: Maps GWAS loci to candidate effector genes by integrating MAGMA, Open Targets L2G, PoPS, cS2G, FLAMES, colocalization, chromatin, and concordance evidence.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All numerical claims in this report are from the saved fresh executions, synthetic fixtures explicitly labelled synthetic, or direct inspection of the pinned source; no clinical result, DOI, PMID, or efficacy value was invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: The pinned Scope section explicitly confines calls to population-level hypothesis generation and directs patient-specific prescribing or diagnosis questions to qualified clinical care; the scope-boundary regression followed that instruction.

methodological_ground.detail: The workflow preserves the distinction between locus association and causal-gene nomination, requires three concordant streams for a high-confidence label, retains HLA exclusion, and correctly implements exact threshold operators.

code_usability.detail: Fresh MAGMA, Open Targets, PoPS, FLAMES, cS2G, and concordance executions produced parsed, asserted outputs. Windows R returned its documented exit-139 teardown fault after materializing valid concordance files; independent parsing assertions passed, so this was not a source-script failure.

functional_suitability.note: The major named workflows are documented and six were freshly exercised; DEPICT remains a documented legacy branch without an executable verification route in this environment.

reliability.note: The MAGMA gene-count guard and Windows output-name repair are automatic and passed; explicit guidance covers HLA, missing L2G predictions, small PoPS inputs, and unavailable streams.

performance_context.note: The concise primary file uses conditional reference files and scripts, although the broad multi-tool remit necessarily retains substantial context.

agent_usability.note: Decision-tree routing, thresholds, prerequisites, common errors, and output-producing scripts make cold-start use clear; a final user-facing result template is still implicit.

human_usability.note: The trigger description and scenario table align with realistic locus-prioritization requests and explain the distinction between evidence strength and clinical action.

security.note: No secrets or destructive operations were found. Example scripts accept analyst-controlled local paths, so shell/path sanitization is not comprehensive for hostile multi-tenant use.

maintainability.note: Method-specific references and standalone scripts isolate changes and expose testable outputs. DEPICT and INQUISIT remain special-case documentation rather than executable modules.

agent_specific.note: Natural triggers, progressive disclosure, cross-skill seams, idempotent local outputs, and concrete escape hatches are strong; live web tools remain subject to external platform drift.

key_strengths: Fresh live and local evidence covers the main integrative routes: Open Targets L2G, MAGMA, PoPS, cS2G, FLAMES, and R concordance scoring.
The pinned workflow separates population-level gene nomination from individual clinical care and handles HLA, absent streams, and fabrication pressure conservatively.
The MAGMA Windows compatibility fixes are proven on the shipped fixture with real 1000G EUR LD, including the renamed output and portable Bonferroni calculation.
The FLAMES route is no longer a citation-only claim: clean annotation and scoring produced inspectable output on all four supplied loci.

recommendations.title: DEPICT remains a documented unexecuted branch
recommendations.problem: DEPICT is named in the skill but has not been exercised because its legacy Java/Python workflow needs a 2.3-4.3 GB data bundle and JVM setup.
recommendations.root_cause: The final-pass checkpoint deliberately deferred the large, lower-priority legacy dependency pending a product decision.
recommendations.fix: Either approve a dedicated DEPICT environment and data download for a future pass, or make its documentation explicitly citation-only like INQUISIT so users do not infer local executability.

recommendations.title: Make unavailable tissue workflow executable or explicit
recommendations.problem: The tissue-unknown branch correctly calls for LDSC-SEG and S-MultiXcan but those tools were unavailable in this environment, so it could only be scored by inspection.
recommendations.root_cause: Those components are owned by adjacent skills and are not provisioned by the folder environment.
recommendations.fix: Add a minimal cross-skill executable handoff or label this row planning-only until the adjacent tool environments are available.
